hero.heading: Music Theory Is Easier Than You Think.
hero.problem: Many people believe music theory is hard, and go to any lengths to avoid learning to read music. It isn't hard. Not if you go about it the right way.

stakes.heading: Does Music Seem Too Complicated?
stakes.text: Are you, or your child, frustrated with learning to read music? Fed up with not being able to finish those theory questions? It isn't you. Most theory books ask you to learn facts by rote and never let you hear what they mean.
items: Learning facts by rote without knowing why
Books that assume you already know half of it
Reading about sounds you never get to hear

faqs.q: Do I need to know anything before I start?
faqs.a: No. Volume 1 starts with the elements of music and assumes nothing at all.

faqs.q: Which exam grades does it cover?
faqs.a: Everything you need for ABRSM Grade 1 and Grade 2 theory. In other courses that is Books 1 and 2, and sometimes 3.

faqs.q: I don't take exams. Is it still for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Rock, jazz or classical, knowing how music is put together makes you better at reading, improvising and composing. And you will enjoy music more when you understand how it works.

faqs.q: What do I need to read it?
faqs.a: An iPad or a Mac with the Apple Books app. The audio, video and quizzes are built into the book, so once it has downloaded you don't need an internet connection.

faqs.q: Can I use it with a class?
faqs.a: Yes. Each student works at their own pace and takes the review at the end of each section, so the differentiation is built in.

courses.heading: Six Courses. One Clear Path From First Note to Grade 5.
courses.lead: Never read a note? Start with the Beginner Course. Then take the grades in order. Each course picks up exactly where the last one stopped, and the path ends at Grade 5, because that is the one most people need.

stakes.heading: Theory Goes Wrong When You Skip a Step
stakes.text: Almost every student I meet who is stuck on theory is stuck for the same reason: there is a gap further back. Key signatures won't make sense until scales do, and scales won't until you are sure of your tones and semitones.
items: Starting at the grade your playing has reached, not your theory
Cramming for Grade 5 because the practical exam needs it
Knowing something is missing, but not what

offer.heading: Six Levels, Taken in Order
offer.needs_review: Draft outline, based on the ABRSM syllabus for each grade. Check it against what each course really covers, then add prices and links.

items.title: Beginner
items.text: The staff, treble and bass clefs, note names and note values. No experience needed. By the end you can read a simple tune.

items.title: Grade 1
items.text: Simple time signatures, rests, ties and dotted notes. The scales and key signatures of C, G, D and F major, tonic triads and your first musical terms.

items.title: Grade 2
items.text: Ledger lines, triplets and new time signatures. More major keys, your first minor keys, and intervals counted from the tonic.

items.title: Grade 3
items.text: Compound time, keys up to four sharps and flats, major, minor and perfect intervals, and moving a tune from one clef to another.

items.title: Grade 4
items.text: The alto clef, double sharps and flats, the chromatic scale, every kind of interval, and the three chords most music is built on.

items.title: Grade 5
items.text: The tenor clef, keys up to six sharps and flats, transposing for instruments, chords and cadences, and reading a score in four parts.

steps.title: Find Your Level
steps.text: Never read music? Take the Beginner Course. Otherwise start a grade below where you think you are. It is quicker than filling gaps later.

steps.title: Take One Course at a Time
steps.text: Work through the lessons in order, and check each idea before you move on to the next.

steps.title: Sit the Exam, or Just Enjoy Knowing
steps.text: By Grade 5 you can read, write and understand most of the music you will ever play.

faqs.q: Which course should I start with?
faqs.a: If you have never read music, the Beginner Course. If you read a little, start at Grade 1 and move quickly through what you know. The gaps are usually further back than people think.

faqs.q: Why do the courses stop at Grade 5?
faqs.a: Because Grade 5 is the one most people need. It is the theory exam the practical boards ask for before the higher grades. These courses are built to get you there with a solid grounding, not to turn you into a professor of harmony.
